messages:
lina: Quick question — when an SLO alert fires in the Console and the routing policy hits a quota limit, what should the default behavior be? Pause notifications? Route to fallback oncall? Requeue to lower-tier channel?

matt: Good one. Current infra will drop into the fallback list if quota exhausted, but we haven't defined the UX for that in the Console. Right now it just says 'delivery deferred'.

olivia: From a UX perspective we should show explicit status: e.g. Delivered | Deferred (quota) | Escalated. Otherwise teams keep DMing us.

harry: Agree. Also want a clear reason string + TTL for the deferral so Console timeline shows when it will retry.

sre-bot: FYI: recent deploy added per-tenant notify-rate caps. Policy: if cap hit -> attempt next tier within same escalation matrix, if none -> mark deferred and enqueue exponential backoff (3 tries).

lina: That backoff behavior is the thing — do we want automatic reroute to a lower-fidelity channel (e.g., email instead of pager) or do we keep strict ordering? Both have tradeoffs.

matt: Tradeoffs: reroute preserves alert visibility but increases noise for lower tiers. Strict ordering preserves noise boundaries but risks missing critical incidents. Maybe make it configurable per SLO alert profile?

ivy: Proposal: add a 'fallback action matrix' in SLO editor with three slots: primary, fallback1, fallback2. Each slot = (channel, min-severity, prefer-escalation-override). Default = [pager, slack, email]. If quota hit, try next slot immediately. If none available, start exponential backoff and mark deferred.

olivia: UI note: keep the editor compact — toggle to expose matrix. Show a small inline preview of what would happen for a simulated quota state.
harry: Also need API-level fields for this so infra can evaluate deterministically: e.g. 
```yaml
notify_profile: 
  primary: pager
  fallbacks:
    - channel: slack
      min_severity: high
    - channel: email
      min_severity: any
  backoff: exponential(5m, max=1h)
```

matt: Sounds good. One more thing — telemetry: we must emit events for every attempted delivery + outcome (delivered, deferred, rerouted) and include reason tags (quota, rate_limit, region-down). That will let Console surface 'notify health' per SLO.

lina: +1 on telemetry. Can we also show a small cost-estimate when teams add a fallback that increases the pager volume? Might help product teams avoid noisy fallbacks.

ivy: Noted. I'll draft a tiny API PR with the fields and wire up a basic simulated preview component. Will open RFC and link it here.

olivia: Thanks — small follow-up: ensure the preview respects tenant-level notify exemptions (quiet windows, maintenance). No surprises during maintenance windows. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

harry: I'll add tests for escalation matrix evaluation and telemetry tags.

sre-bot: deploy scheduled: feature/notify-matrix -> staging at 2024-11-14T03:00Z (automated).

lina: Perfect. Thanks all — looking forward to the RFC.
